title: Apothecary Melchior and the Ghost of Rataskaevu Street
author: Indrek Hargla
description: The first of Indrek Hargla’s mysteries set in medieval Tallinn, solved by Melchior, the apothecary on Town Hall Square. The real Town Hall Pharmacy has been dispensing medicine since at least 1422.

title: Treading Air
author: Jaan Kross
description: Paigallend: Jaan Kross, Estonia’s best-known novelist, follows a gifted Tallinn man through the brief independence of the 1920s and 1930s and the Soviet and Nazi occupations that ended it.

title: When the Doves Disappeared
author: Sofi Oksanen
description: A novel by the Finnish-Estonian writer Sofi Oksanen about two cousins in Estonia through the Soviet, Nazi, and second Soviet occupations, and the betrayals each regime demanded. The KGB watched foreign guests from the Viru hotel.

title: Pobeda 1946: A Car Called Victory
author: Ilmar Taska
description: A boy in Tallinn in 1946 is fascinated by a stranger’s new Soviet car, unaware the driver is a secret police officer watching his family. A tense, short novel about fear just after the war.

title: The Baltic Revolution
author: Anatol Lieven
description: Journalist Anatol Lieven’s account of how Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania broke free of the Soviet Union, written from reporting in all three countries, with the history behind it.

title: A History of the Baltic States
author: Andres Kasekamp
description: Estonian historian Andres Kasekamp’s short, clear history of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, from the medieval crusades and the Hanseatic towns to independence and joining the EU.
